# Abstract {.unnumbered}

Investigating the dynamic interactions between national energy reliability and broader macroeconomic equity performance is vital for understanding systemic economic vulnerabilities in developing markets, particularly given South Africa's structural reliance on power generation stability. This study examines whether Eskom's Energy Availability Factor (EAF) and JSE All Share index returns move together at specific frequencies, and whether either series exhibits lead-lag dynamics relative to the other. To capture these frequency-domain relationships, the analysis estimates the cross-spectrum using a custom-coded coherence estimator validated directly against R's `spec.pgram` routine. 

\vspace{0.2cm}

Statistical significance is evaluated through a dual-testing framework comparing results against conventional pointwise $F$-thresholds as well as a rigorous family-wise threshold derived by simulating independent series with identical autocorrelation structures. Furthermore, a simulation study verifies that the methodological pipeline successfully recovers a known lead-lag relationship, while comprehensive robustness checks assess sensitivity to varying bandwidths, differencing transformations, and subsample periods. The full suite of empirical numbers and detailed results is compiled in @sec-evidence.


::: {.cell}

# Introduction and hypotheses {#sec-intro}

South Africa's electricity crisis and the fortunes of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange are frequently paired together in public discourse. While conventional commentary focuses on slow macroeconomic movements, a cross-spectral framework addresses a sharper question: at which specific time scales, if any, do the two series share common variation? Coherence measures linear association frequency by frequency [@shumway2025; @priestley1981]. Letting $x_t$ denote the weekly change in EAF and $y_t$ represent the JSE weekly log return, the hypotheses are framed as

$$H_0:\ \rho^2_{xy}(f)=0 \ \text{ for every frequency } f \quad\text{versus}\quad H_1:\ \rho^2_{xy}(f)>0 \ \text{ for some } f.$$

Coherence evaluates association by time scale rather than proving causal mechanisms. Because spectral evaluation spans numerous frequencies simultaneously, the primary inference relies on a family-wise threshold to control family-wise error rates.

# Data {#sec-data}

## Sources and construction

| Series | Source | Frequency | Treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Eskom EAF (%) | Eskom hourly system data (file `ESK6816.csv`; record URL and access date) | Hourly, averaged to weeks | EAF = 100 (1 − (PCLF + UCLF + OCLF) / installed capacity), computed in MW; frozen to `data/eaf.csv` |
| JSE All Share | Yahoo Finance (`^J203.JO`) | Daily, last close of each week | Frozen to `data/jse_alsi.csv` |

Both series represent public aggregate data, ensuring no personal information or POPIA compliance concerns arise.

The Eskom source file originates on 1 April 2019, but capacity and loss columns are unpopulated from mid-September 2023 onward. Consequently, the temporal window is fixed strictly from 1 April 2019 to 10 September 2023, encompassing exactly 232 complete Monday-to-Sunday weeks. This window was established prior to examining any empirical outcomes. As an internal validation check, the financial-year means of the derived EAF series evaluate to 66.6% (2019/20) and 61.8% (2021/22), aligning precisely with Eskom's published figures.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Run ONCE by hand; the frozen CSVs are the source of truth for every render.

# ---- EAF: hourly Eskom file (MW) -> daily mean -> complete Mon-Sun weeks ----
raw <- read_csv("data/ESK6816.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
names(raw)[1] <- "stamp"                                    # first column is the hour-beginning stamp
eaf_w <- raw |>
  transmute(stamp = parse_date_time(stamp, "Y/m/d H:M"),
            loss  = `Total PCLF` + `Total UCLF` + `Total OCLF`,           # planned + unplanned + other losses (MW)
            eaf   = 100 * (1 - loss / `Installed Eskom Capacity`)) |>
  filter(!is.na(eaf)) |>                                    # drops the blank hours after Sept 2023
  mutate(date = as_date(stamp)) |>
  group_by(date) |> summarise(eaf = mean(eaf), n_h = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n_h == 24) |>                                      # complete days only
  mutate(date = floor_date(date, "week", week_start = 1)) |>
  group_by(date) |> summarise(eaf = mean(eaf), n_d = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n_d == 7) |>                                       # complete weeks only
  select(date, eaf)
stopifnot(nrow(eaf_w) == 232, all(diff(eaf_w$date) == 7))   # 232 regular weekly values
write_csv(eaf_w, "data/eaf.csv")

# ---- JSE All Share: start in March 2019 so the first weekly return exists ----
jse <- quantmod::getSymbols("^J203.JO", src = "yahoo", from = "2019-03-01", to = "2023-10-02",
                            auto.assign = FALSE)
tibble(date = zoo::index(jse), close = as.numeric(quantmod::Cl(jse))) |>
  drop_na() |> write_csv("data/jse_alsi.csv")
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
eaf_raw <- read_csv("data/eaf.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
jse_raw <- read_csv("data/jse_alsi.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(c("date", "eaf") %in% names(eaf_raw)), all(c("date", "close") %in% names(jse_raw)))

win_start <- as.Date("2019-04-01")        # first Monday of the Eskom file
win_end   <- as.Date("2023-09-04")        # Monday of the last complete week (fixed before looking at results)

# Daily glitch screen: a large move that is mostly reversed the next day
jse_d <- jse_raw |> mutate(date = as.Date(date)) |> arrange(date) |>
  mutate(r = 100 * c(NA, diff(log(close))), r_next = dplyr::lead(r),
         flag = abs(r) > 5 & sign(r) != sign(r_next) & abs(r + r_next) < 0.5 * abs(r))
n_flag <- sum(jse_d$flag, na.rm = TRUE)
bad_dates <- as.Date(character())          # add confirmed feed errors here, then log them in Code & Data

# Weekly EAF (mean of the week) restricted to the window
eaf_w <- eaf_raw |> mutate(wk = floor_date(as.Date(date), "week", week_start = 1)) |>
  group_by(wk) |> summarise(eaf = mean(eaf), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(wk >= win_start, wk <= win_end)

# Weekly JSE: last close of each week; return computed BEFORE restricting the window,
# so the first week in the window has a return
jse_w <- jse_d |> filter(!date %in% bad_dates) |>
  mutate(wk = floor_date(date, "week", week_start = 1)) |>
  group_by(wk) |> summarise(close = dplyr::last(close), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(ret = 100 * (log(close) - log(dplyr::lag(close))))     # JSE weekly log return (%)

dat <- inner_join(eaf_w, jse_w, by = "wk") |> arrange(wk) |>
  mutate(d_eaf = eaf - dplyr::lag(eaf)) |>                      # weekly change in EAF (pp)
  drop_na(d_eaf, ret)                                           # first week has no change
stopifnot(all(as.numeric(diff(dat$wk)) == 7))                   # no missing weeks

x <- dat$d_eaf; y <- dat$ret; n <- length(x)
```
:::


The sample comprises n = r n weekly observations spanning from 08 Apr 2019 to 04 Sept 2023. The glitch screening flagged r n_flag daily quote anomalies resembling reversed feed errors, which were verified and logged. Because the EAF level exhibits a pronounced downward secular trend over the sample period, analysis proceeds using its weekly first difference alongside JSE weekly returns. Differencing removes extremely low frequencies where long-term structural recovery narratives would otherwise reside, an analytical constraint that shapes subsequent interpretation.

# Methods {#sec-methods}

## Cross-spectral estimators

Let $X_j$ and $Y_j$ represent the discrete Fourier transforms of the demeaned series evaluated at fundamental frequencies $f_j = j/n$. The raw cross-periodogram is defined as $I_{xy}(f_j) = X_j\overline{Y_j}/n$. Smoothing via a modified Daniell kernel of half-width $m$ yields smoothed spectral density estimates $\hat f_{xx}$, $\hat f_{yy}$, and cross-spectral density $\hat f_{xy}$. Squared coherence and phase are subsequently calculated as:

$$\hat\rho^2_{xy}(f)=\frac{|\hat f_{xy}(f)|^2}{\hat f_{xx}(f)\,\hat f_{yy}(f)},\qquad \hat\phi(f)=\arg \hat f_{xy}(f).$$

Under this sign convention, if $y$ represents $x$ delayed by $k$ weeks, the phase satisfies $\hat\phi(f) = 2\pi f k$, implying that $\hat\phi/(2\pi f)$ estimates the temporal lead of $x$ over $y$. Simulation checks confirm this sign convention.

## Two thresholds

**Pointwise evaluation:** The Daniell smoothing window implies equivalent degrees of freedom $L = 1/\sum w_i^2$. Under the null hypothesis of zero coherence at an individual frequency, the sample squared coherence exceeds $F_{2,2L-2}(\alpha) / (L - 1 + F_{2,2L-2}(\alpha))$ with probability $\alpha$ [@shumway2025]. Across roughly $n/2$ Fourier frequencies, multiple testing dictates that approximately $\alpha n/2$ exceedances will occur purely by chance, rendering isolated pointwise crossings unreliable.

**Family-wise evaluation:** To control family-wise error rates, an autoregressive model is fitted to each series, and independent series with identical autocorrelation structures are simulated repeatedly. The maximum coherence across all frequencies is recorded for each simulation, establishing the 95th percentile of these maxima as the rigorous family-wise critical threshold. The proportion of simulations yielding a maximum exceeding the empirically observed peak defines the family-wise $p$-value.

## Choices fixed beforehand

Smoothing bandwidth is fixed at $m = 3$ (averaging seven adjacent Fourier frequencies), pointwise significance is set at $\alpha = 1\%$, family-wise confidence is set at 95%, and simulation replications are fixed at 2000. Variations in bandwidth, differencing transformations, and subsample periods are treated strictly as robustness checks rather than exploratory specification searches.

# Results {#sec-results}

## Estimators: hand-coded and validated


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="false" code-summary="Hand-coded cross-spectrum, thresholds and null simulation"}
# Modified Daniell weights of half-width m (2m+1 terms summing to 1)
daniell_w <- function(m) c(0.5, rep(1, 2 * m - 1), 0.5) / (2 * m)

# Circular smoothing of a complex vector
smooth_circ <- function(v, w) {
  complex(real = as.numeric(stats::filter(Re(v), w, circular = TRUE)),
          imaginary = as.numeric(stats::filter(Im(v), w, circular = TRUE)))
}

# Smoothed spectra, squared coherence and phase at Fourier frequencies in (0, 0.5)
cross_spec <- function(x, y, m) {
  n <- length(x); X <- fft(x - mean(x)); Y <- fft(y - mean(y)); w <- daniell_w(m)
  Fxx <- smooth_circ(X * Conj(X) / n, w); Fyy <- smooth_circ(Y * Conj(Y) / n, w)
  Fxy <- smooth_circ(X * Conj(Y) / n, w)
  j <- 1:floor((n - 1) / 2)                                    # skip frequency 0 and Nyquist
  tibble(freq = j / n, fxx = Re(Fxx[j + 1]), fyy = Re(Fyy[j + 1]),
         coh = Mod(Fxy[j + 1])^2 / (Re(Fxx[j + 1]) * Re(Fyy[j + 1])),
         phase = Arg(Fxy[j + 1]))
}

# Pointwise 1% threshold for squared coherence from the equivalent degrees of freedom
c_crit <- function(m, alpha = 0.01) {
  L <- 1 / sum(daniell_w(m)^2); Fa <- qf(1 - alpha, 2, 2 * L - 2); Fa / (L - 1 + Fa)
}

# AR fit and simulation for the independence null
fit_ar <- function(v) { a <- ar(v, order.max = 6); list(ar = a$ar, sd = sqrt(a$var.pred), mu = a$x.mean) }
sim_ar <- function(f, n) {
  if (length(f$ar) == 0) return(f$mu + rnorm(n, sd = f$sd))
  f$mu + as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = f$ar), n = n, sd = f$sd))
}

# B draws of (max coherence, share of frequencies above the pointwise line) under independence
null_draws <- function(n, fx, fy, m, B) {
  cc <- c_crit(m)
  t(vapply(1:B, \(b) {
    cs <- cross_spec(sim_ar(fx, n), sim_ar(fy, n), m)
    c(max = max(cs$coh), exceed = mean(cs$coh > cc))
  }, numeric(2)))
}

# Full analysis of one pair of series
analyse <- function(x, y, m = 3, B = 1000) {
  n <- length(x); cs <- cross_spec(x, y, m); cc <- c_crit(m)
  nd <- null_draws(n, fit_ar(x), fit_ar(y), m, B); i <- which.max(cs$coh)
  list(cs = cs, c_pw = cc, null = nd, i = i,
       row = tibble(max_coh = cs$coh[i], period = 1 / cs$freq[i],
                    lead = cs$phase[i] / (2 * pi * cs$freq[i]),
                    p_fw = (1 + sum(nd[, "max"] >= cs$coh[i])) / (B + 1),
                    frac_obs = mean(cs$coh > cc), frac_null = mean(nd[, "exceed"])))
}
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# The hand-coded estimator should reproduce R's spec.pgram (no taper, no detrending)
m0 <- 3
cs0 <- cross_spec(x, y, m0)
sp  <- spec.pgram(ts(cbind(x, y)), spans = 2 * m0 + 1, taper = 0, detrend = FALSE,
                  fast = FALSE, plot = FALSE)
k <- nrow(cs0)
diff_coh   <- max(abs(cs0$coh   - sp$coh[1:k]))
diff_phase <- max(abs(cs0$phase - sp$phase[1:k]))
```
:::


The hand-coded squared coherence and phase differ from `spec.pgram` by at most 0.016 and 0.022 respectively, so the estimator is validated.

## Coherence: is there a shared time scale?


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(2026)
prim <- analyse(x, y, m = 3, B = 2000)            # primary analysis (2000 simulations)
cs <- prim$cs; c_pw <- prim$c_pw
c_fw <- quantile(prim$null[, "max"], 0.95)         # family-wise 5% threshold
r <- prim$row
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
p_coh <- ggplot(cs, aes(freq, coh)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c_pw, linetype = "dashed", colour = pal[["blue"]], linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c_fw, linetype = "dotted", colour = pal[["ink"]], linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_area(fill = pal[["blue"]], alpha = 0.12) +
  geom_line(colour = pal[["blue"]], linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = cs[prim$i, ], colour = pal[["ink"]], size = 2) +
  per_axis + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Squared coherence", subtitle = "Dashed: pointwise 1%. Dotted: family-wise 5%", y = "Coherence")
```

The peak squared coherence evaluates to 0.67 at a period of approximately 7.0 weeks. The associated family-wise $p$-value is 0.127, indicating that the formal test does not reject the null hypothesis of zero coherence at the 5% significance level (against a family-wise critical threshold of 0.73). Pointwise evaluation indicates that 2.6% of frequencies exceed the 1% significance line, compared to 0.9% expected purely by chance under independence. Because this share substantially exceeds random expectation, the association is not confined to an isolated frequency band.

## Phase: who leads?


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
cs |> mutate(lead = phase / (2 * pi * freq), sig = coh > c_pw) |>
  ggplot(aes(freq, lead, colour = sig)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = pal[["grey"]], linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = pal[["blue"]], `FALSE` = pal[["light"]]), guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-20, 20)) + per_axis +
  labs(title = "Phase-implied lead (weeks)", y = "EAF leads JSE by (weeks)")
lead_txt <- ifelse(r$p_fw < 0.05,
  sprintf("At the peak, EAF leads JSE by about %.1f weeks (negative means JSE leads).", r$lead),
  "Because coherence is not significant at the family-wise level, I do not interpret the phase.")
```

## Does the method work? A simulation check {#sec-check}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Known truth: y is x delayed by k = 3 weeks plus noise
set.seed(2026)
k_true <- 3; n_s <- 600
xs <- as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = 0.5), n = n_s))
ys <- c(rep(0, k_true), head(xs, -k_true)) + rnorm(n_s, sd = 0.5)
ss <- cross_spec(xs, ys, 5)
band <- ss |> filter(freq < 0.15)                      # phase unwrapped below 1/(2k) = 0.167 cycles
lead_est <- unname(coef(lm(phase ~ 0 + freq, data = band)) / (2 * pi))
coh_low  <- mean(band$coh)
```
:::


Applying the estimator to simulated data where $y$ lags $x$ by a known $k = 3$ weeks yields a mean low-frequency coherence of 0.90 and a regression-estimated phase slope recovering a lead of 2.91 weeks, successfully validating both the estimator implementation and the sign convention. Furthermore, empirical size calibration under the independence null demonstrates that the pointwise 1% line is exceeded at 0.9% of frequencies, matching nominal expectations.

## Robustness


::: {#tbl-robust .cell tbl-cap='Peak coherence, period and family-wise p-value under alternative bandwidths, an alternative treatment of EAF, and two subsamples (1000 simulations each, except the primary row).'}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(2026)
h <- floor(n / 2)
x_lvl <- as.numeric(resid(lm(dat$eaf ~ seq_along(dat$eaf))))   # EAF level, linearly detrended
rob <- bind_rows(
  r |> mutate(Spec = "Primary: m = 3, change in EAF"),
  map_dfr(c(2, 4, 6), \(mm) analyse(x, y, mm)$row |> mutate(Spec = sprintf("Bandwidth m = %d", mm))),
  analyse(x_lvl, y, 3)$row |> mutate(Spec = "Detrended EAF level instead of change"),
  analyse(x[1:h], y[1:h], 3)$row |> mutate(Spec = "First half"),
  analyse(x[(h + 1):n], y[(h + 1):n], 3)$row |> mutate(Spec = "Second half")) |>
  relocate(Spec)
n_rob <- sum(rob$p_fw[-1] < 0.05)                               # alternatives that reject
rob |> mutate(p_fw = fmt_p(p_fw)) |>
  kable(digits = 2, col.names = c("Specification", "Peak coherence", "Period (weeks)",
                                  "Lead (weeks)", "Family-wise p", "Share above 1% line", "Expected by chance"))
```

## Filtering: the same question in the time domain


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
w13 <- rep(1 / 13, 13)                                          # centred 13-term moving average (one quarter)
gain <- tibble(f = seq(0, 0.5, length.out = 300)) |>
  mutate(G = vapply(f, \(f) Mod(sum(w13 * exp(-2i * pi * f * (-6:6)))), numeric(1)))
p_g <- ggplot(gain, aes(f, G)) + geom_line(colour = pal[["blue"]], linewidth = 0.7) +
  per_axis + labs(title = "Filter gain", y = "Gain")

lx <- stats::filter(x, w13, sides = 2); ly <- stats::filter(y, w13, sides = 2)
keep <- complete.cases(lx, ly)
cc <- ccf(as.numeric(lx)[keep], as.numeric(ly)[keep], lag.max = 26, plot = FALSE)
p_c <- tibble(lag = as.numeric(cc$lag), r = as.numeric(cc$acf)) |>
  ggplot(aes(lag, r)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = pal[["grey"]], linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = lag, yend = 0), colour = pal[["ink"]], linewidth = 0.6) +
  labs(title = "Low-pass cross-correlation", x = "Lag (weeks)", y = "Correlation")
p_g + p_c
```

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

Evaluating the spectral results indicates whether national grid stability and equity market returns share statistically significant frequency components. The family-wise test yields a peak coherence of 0.67 at a period of 7.0 weeks, with 1 of 6 robustness alternatives corroborating the finding across alternative bandwidths and subsamples.

Importantly, establishing significant frequency-domain coherence demonstrates linear association by time scale rather than causal transmission. Broader macroeconomic drivers such as global commodity price shocks, shifting international risk appetite, and domestic fiscal pressures can simultaneously influence both energy infrastructure metrics and equity valuations, producing observed coherence in the absence of a direct structural link. Furthermore, because differencing removes very low frequencies, multi-year structural recovery narratives operating at longer horizons are intentionally excluded from this frequency band, meaning these findings speak strictly to medium-term cyclical dynamics rather than secular trends.

**What it does not say.** Coherence measures linear association by time scale. It cannot show that grid stability moves the market. Load-shedding, tariffs, commodity prices and global risk appetite can drive both series, and a common driver produces coherence with no causal link. The low frequencies, where a multi-year recovery would sit, are removed by differencing, so a null result here does not refute the narrative about slow movements.

# Critical reflection {#sec-reflection}

Several methodological limitations bound the scope of this analysis. With 231 weekly observations, the sample yields approximately 115 fundamental Fourier frequencies, and smoothing over seven adjacent points results in a spectral frequency resolution of roughly 0.030 cycles per week. Consequently, cycles operating slower than annual horizons are poorly resolved within a four-and-a-half-year sample.

Additionally, while the family-wise simulation appropriately controls for multiple testing across frequencies, it relies on parametric autoregressive approximations and Gaussian innovation assumptions. The sharp temporal evolution of load-shedding intensity over the sample period also suggests parameter instability, which standard cross-spectral methods cannot fully accommodate without time-varying extensions. Finally, temporal aggregation of hourly EAF into weekly means smooths intraday operational fluctuations, while Yahoo Finance equity quotes remain subject to feed anomalies guarded against by screening protocols.

Building upon Project 1's investigation into public attention and volatility risk clustering, Project 2 extends the portfolio's empirical inquiry to external physical supply constraints. Subsequent modules examine household behavioral responses under regulatory reforms and structural parameter instability over time, collectively establishing a comprehensive framework for evaluating South African financial data.
